To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the supplementation of weaned pigs with CTC and copper differentially impacted the presence and quantity (i.e., copy number) of the various tetrocycline, ceftiofuir, and copper resistance genes.

the supplementation of chlortracycline and copper differentially impacted the gut microbial community of weaned piglets and resulted in a decrease in the overall prevalence of antimicrobial resistance, while increasing the prevalence and gene quantity of some resistance genes.

the presence and quantity in the fecal community of pigs of tetracycline and cephalosporins resistance genes were affected by CTC supplementation, whereas copper supplementation affected the presence and quantity only of copper resistance genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of CTS and copper supplementation on gut microbial ecology and antimicrobial resistance genes, and how these factors impact the gut microbial ecology and health status of food animals.
the effects of CTS and copper supplementation on antimicrobial resistance genes.
the effect of CTC and Cu on the prevalence and quantity, but not the diversity of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes in the gut of weaned pigs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CTC and copper, either alone or in combination, differentially impact the prevalence and quantity (gene copies) of the various teth and blaCMY- 2 genes in the gut microbial community.

the use of copper and copper plus C TC supplementation differentially impacted on the prevalence and quantity (gene copy number) of the tetracycline and ceftiofur resistance genes, resulting in a less gene diversity in the gut microbial population.
copper supplementation increased the prevalence of tetA and decreased the prevalence and quantity (gene copy number) of tetB.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CTC and copper have differential impacts on the gut microbial ecology in weaned pigs.
CTC supplementation decreased the diversity of tet genes and copper supplementation increased the diversity of tet and blaCMY- 2 genes.
CTC and copper have differential effects on the presence and abundance of antimicrobial resistance gene in weaned pigs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gut microbial community of pigs is a complex and dynamic system that is influenced by the presence of antibiotics and other antimicrobials.

the use of CTC in feed may not only increase the presence of tetracycline resistant genes in the gut of pigs, but may also select for the proliferation of other resistance genes, including those that confer resistance to copper.
CTC and copper can impact the presence and quantity, but not the overall diversity of antimicrobial resistance gene presence in the fecal bacterial communities of pigs.
